newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-BOURSE SAYS GETS 80 PCT OF SHARE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-BOURSE SAYS GETS 80 PCT OF SHARE TRADE.

text.p: The turnover of Tallinn stock exchange accounts for 80 percent of Estonia's total stock market turnover, bourse managing director Helo Meigas said Wednesday.
"Almost the whole trade goes through the stock exchange," Meigas told Reuters in an interview.

The turnover of Estonian shares was 1.4 billion kroons in March and the Tallinn stock exchange saw trade of 1.26 billion kroons. In Latvia, the OTC market accounted for 44.8 percent of total turnover in March.

Shares quoted on the over-the-counter market include textile firm Klementi, Leks Insurance, which is soon to join the stock exchange, Emex, a metals trader, Liviko, Estonia's largest producer of alchohol, and various bonds.
Stocks which are also quoted on the stock exchange or traded on the free market account for one to four percent of OTC trade.
Meigas said that Tallinn stock exchange accounted for 90 percent of actual trades.
The high share of stock exchange in total turnover has been stable since last October, Meigas said. The size of OTC trade market was about 30 percent before October, she added.
"The opening of the free-market has played an important role here," she said.
The companies on the free market have no listing obligations but use the infrastructure of the bourse.
"Market participants have realised that it is more convenient to make deals through the stock exchange," she added.
